title: Northern Red Oak: Old Red Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The North American oak that turns scarlet in autumn. Toronto bought and demolished a house in 2020 to save Zhelevo, a red oak of roughly 300 years.
intro: Northern red oak is the oak of eastern North America, and Europe planted it for one thing: nothing native turns that colour in autumn. Brussels Environment's own walking route through the Parc d'Egmont gives up on describing its red oak and tells you to come back in autumn instead. At home the old ones are older. In 2020 Toronto's city council bought a private house on Coral Gable Drive and tore it down to save Zhelevo, an oak of roughly 300 years left from the savannah along the old Carrying Place trail. Toronto's official tree, in Kew Gardens, is 5.3 metres round with one limb sagging to the grass. In Europe, Prague's stands on the island where the city's archers used to practise, and the Baarn oak, roughly 175 years old, wears a ring carrying words the municipality asked its residents to write in 2021.
